external_entities.name: member
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop

external_entities.name: member phone
external_entities.description: A phone used by a member to run the mobile app.

external_entities.name: member browser
external_entities.description: A browser used by a member to sign in and approve consent.
external_entities.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

external_entities.name: partnerships team
external_entities.description: The team that registers partner apps.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our partnerships team registers each partner app by hand

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: Mobile application used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.
processes.notes: The text does not state whether the app sends a PKCE challenge. The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: Authorization server handling member sign-in, consent, authorization codes, refresh tokens and access tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: The member sign-in cookie has no decided idle timeout.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: API called by the mobile app and partner apps to access the points ledger.
processes.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
processes.notes: It checks JWT signatures with a public key downloaded at startup, but does not check the client or audience.

processes.name: partner app
processes.description: A web application run by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
processes.notes: Each partner app receives a client ID and client secret and is given every scope.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: Web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: Refresh tokens remain in the database when an account is closed. Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, and not which member approved it. Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store
data_stores.notes: Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: Member interaction with the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: PKCE challenge status is not recorded.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API using an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The member's browser accesses the authorization server sign-in page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: The member approves the listed scopes through the authorization server sign-in flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: approves a consent screen that lists the scopes
data_flows.notes: The member interaction is represented directly because the browser page has sign-in and consent behavior through the authorization server.

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The text describes the browser as the initiator of the return to the redirect URI.

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: The partner app requests tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The client secret is sent in the request body.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret and authorization code

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: The partner app accesses member points through the rewards API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a meal-planning service that shows a member's points
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: disconnect app
data_flows.description: The mobile app requests disconnection of a partner app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app
data_flows.notes: The resulting deletion of the partner app's refresh token is recorded on the authorization server to identity database flow.
data_flows.data_description: partner connection and refresh-token deletion request

data_flows.name: manage identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and retrieves identity, authorization and token data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.notes: The connection protocol and encryption in transit are not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: update ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: The connection protocol and encryption in transit are not recorded.

data_flows.name: write logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes received requests and headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_flows.notes: The connection protocol and encryption in transit are not recorded.

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: The connection protocol and encryption in transit are not recorded.

data_flows.name: get token
data_flows.description: The support console obtains access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account. It takes access tokens from the same authorization server
data_flows.notes: unknown

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's own cloud account where the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: member phones
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing members' phones, outside the organization's cloud account.

trust_boundaries.name: partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it contains member account information, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include personal information and credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it contains member-linked balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store is confidential because request headers can contain bearer access tokens and other credentials.
assumptions.basis: The rewards API writes every request it receives, headers included, and its requests use access tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The description says the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The description says the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
